t: After Li Hongzhang ignored his reform petition in 1894, Sun spent most of seventeen years in exile raising money among overseas Chinese for a series of failed uprisings against the Qing.
When the Wuchang uprising of 1911 brought down the dynasty, he was elected provisional president but gave the office to Yuan Shikai in 1912 in return for the emperor's abdication.
Fighting Yuan and the warlords from a base in Guangzhou, he allied with the Soviet Union and the Chinese Communist Party, and both the Republic of China and the People's Republic now claim him.
dyk: Sun's best-known name in Chinese, Sun Zhongshan, comes from Nakayama, the Japanese pseudonym Tōten Miyazaki gave him while he hid in Japan; his birthplace was renamed Zhongshan after his death.
ev: Sun graduates from the Hong Kong College of Medicine for Chinese
His petition to Li Hongzhang is ignored and he founds the Revive China Society in Hawaii
The First Guangzhou Uprising fails and Sun goes into exile
He forms the Tongmenghui with Chinese students in Tokyo
Sun takes office as provisional president, then resigns in favour of Yuan Shikai
The Second Revolution against Yuan fails and Sun flees to Japan
The Sun-Joffe Manifesto opens his alliance with the Soviet Union
Sun dies of cancer in Beijing

f.born: 12 November 1866 in the village of Cuiheng, Xiangshan County (now Zhongshan), Guangdong; son of Sun Dacheng, a poor farmer, tailor and porter, and Madame Yang; Hakka and Cantonese
f.died: 12 March 1925 in Beijing, aged 58, of cancer; long reported as liver cancer, the autopsy found a gallbladder cancer that had spread to the liver
f.role: Physician, licensed 1892; founder of the Revive China Society (1894) and leader of the Tongmenghui (1905); provisional president of the Republic of China, 1912; leader of the Kuomintang; head of the military government in Guangzhou from 1921
f.known: the 1911 Revolution; first provisional president of the Republic of China; founding the Kuomintang; the Three Principles of the People; the First United Front with the Soviet Union and the Chinese Communist Party; the Whampoa Military Academy
